paragraphs: Swiftly sells a cloud platform to public transit agencies for sharing real-time passenger information, running daily operations, and improving service performance. The company puts its customer count above 200 agencies. Those agencies are described as large and small, around the globe.

The platform combines GTFS schedule data with whatever real-time vehicle location feed an agency already has. It then analyzes billions of data points to say where a vehicle was, where it is, and where it will be next. Operations staff use it to make real-time adjustments for on-time performance and headway adherence. Schedulers work from actual run times, vehicle speeds, and dwell times. APIs push the same data out to rider-facing apps, vehicle hardware, and internal tools.

Customer service teams are another audience, answering rider questions from the same information. The site carries comments from transit staff, including an operations technology lead at the MBTA in Boston. Another comes from a transportation planner at MDOT MTA in Baltimore. Jonny Simkin co-founded the company and is its chief executive. Swiftly describes itself as a transit reliability platform meant to keep public transportation a fast and attractive alternative to the private vehicle.
